insights.insight: 12,302 cryptographically verified receipts confirm purchases happened — no inference, no modeling. At $990K in verified GMV, this dataset represents the kind of closed-loop purchase confirmation that probabilistic cookie-based targeting cannot replicate.

The network sits $9,485 from $1M in verified commerce volume, with recent 4-hour cycle inflows ranging $3K–$5K. The milestone crossing is a concrete proof-of-scale moment, not a projection — the gap is smaller than a single strong inflow cycle.

insights.topic: Velocity deceleration is real but not a demand collapse
insights.insight: Token velocity dropped to 0.819x — the steepest single-cycle decline recorded — but the mechanical cause is a rolling 7-day window clearing an unusually high-volume week from April 8–12, not a behavioral drop-off. Acceleration holding at 1.004x means the contraction is not yet compounding.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion now reaches rural and non-metro America
insights.insight: Active CBSAs have expanded to 21 metro areas including non-metro geographies across WI, NC, RI, OH, CA, ID, NE, IA, ME — markets where physical retail is dominant and digital targeting data is historically thin. This is a meaningful coverage signal for brands with national or rural distribution.

insights.topic: Category breadth spans physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and SaaS
insights.insight: The protocol now captures receipts across five distinct commerce categories, with SaaS subscriptions entering the dataset on April 9 — the first non-physical-commerce signal in network history. For brand marketers, this means purchase context extends beyond store trips into recurring digital spend.

A total endpoint blackout on April 14 — all 16 endpoints down simultaneously — resolved within roughly 12 hours, with three new CBSAs added in the recovery cycle. The system's ability to resume geographic diffusion post-outage is a relevant reliability data point for any brand considering this as infrastructure.
